headline: Recommended City Council accept $759,000 conservation restriction on Magnolia Reserve land, plus a new utility pole on Madison Avenue.
summary: Greenbelt would own the Magnolia Reserve land, about 94 acres, and the city would hold a conservation restriction on it. Councilors also recommended a National Grid permit for a new utility pole on Madison Avenue, with six Public Works conditions.
decisions: Recommended National Grid pole permit on Madison Avenue, 3-0, with six conditions.
Recommended City Council accept the $759,000 conservation restriction on Magnolia Reserve land, 3-0.

plain_text:
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 1 of 6
Planning & Development Standing Committee
Wednesday, November 18, 2026 – 6:00 p.m.
City Hall
1st Floor Council Conference Room
9 Dale Avenue
Gloucester, MA 01930
-Minutes-
Planning & Development Committee Present: Chair, Councilor Jason Grow; Councilor Tony Gross;
Councilor Hannah Kimberley
Absent: Vice Chair, Councilor Dylan Benson
Also Present: General Counsel, Suzanne Egan; Planning Director, Gregg Cademartori; Legislative
Aide, Lynds Jones
This meeting was conducted in person and remotely through ZOOM
Councilor Grow called the P&D meeting to order at 6:00 p.m.
Councilor Grow announced the names of the P&D Committee members in attendance.
1. PP2026-012: Petition by National Grid to install 1 JO Pole on Madison Avenue beginning at a 
point approximately 120 feet West of the centerline of the intersection of Madison Avenue and 
Acacia Street and continuing approximately 19 feet in a Northern direction. Proposed 
installation of pole #4590-50 with a sidewalk fixtured anchor and guy wire. Removal of 
secondary conductor from pole #5490 to pole #5485 and installation of secondary conductor 
from new pole #5490-50 to pole #5485. Gloucester, MA.
 Public Hearing Opened: 6:01 p.m.
 Speaking in Favor: Ismail Mikou, 44 River Street, Beverly stated that the proposed pole was being
installed to correct the route of wires that currently went over the roof of 44 Madison Avenue. He
stated that this was no longer best practice, and that rerouting the wires would improve safety. He
stated that the new pole would have a sidewalk anchor and guy wire and the installation would take
about four hours, and there would be no power outage.
Ismail Mikou shared his screen. He stated that the black dot was the proposed location for the new
pole, and the red line was where wires were currently passing over 44 Madison Avenue.
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 2 of 6
 Speaking in Opposition: None.
 Communications: Legislative Aide, Lynds Jones read the following memos from the DPW
Director, Michael Hale:
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 3 of 6
 Questions from Councilors to Applicants/Staff: Councilor Gross asked where the guy wire would
be located. Ismail Mikou stated that the guy wire would be a sidewalk anchor and would not block
the sidewalk.
David Quinn, 10 Acacia Street, asked Ismail Mikou to contact the gas department of National Grid
as there had been a noticeable gas smell in the neighborhood.
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 4 of 6
 Public Hearing Closed: 6:15 p.m.
Summary of Discussion: None.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor
Kimberley, the Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the
City Council permit Massachusetts Electric Company d/b/a National Grid, to locate poles, wires and
fixtures, including the necessary sustaining and protecting fixtures, along and across the public way,
National Grid to install 1 JO pole on Madison Ave beginning at a point approximately 120 feet West of the
centerline of the intersection of Madison Ave and Acacia Street and continuing approximately 19 feet in a
Northern direction. Proposed installation of pole #4590-50 with a sidewalk fixtured anchor and guy wire.
Removal of secondary conductor from pole #5490 to pole #5485 and installation of secondary conductor
from new pole #5490-50 to pole #5485. Gloucester, MA.- as shown on a plan included in the application
dated September 1, 2026 – with the following conditions:
1. Notification to the Department of Public Works 72 hours in advance of the proposed 
work. A construction schedule will be prepared by the applicant for review and 
acceptance by the Department of Public Works.
2. In the absence of a detailed construction plan, the Department of Public Works requests: 
all proposed conduits and appurtenances shall be placed so as to cause minimum conflict 
with existing underground utility services.
3. All excavations must be secured at all times.
4. All excavated trenches shall be patched flush with the surrounding asphalt using hot mix 
asphalt binder at the end of each work day, to minimize pedestrian hazards. Asphalt shall 
be applied in two lifts of 2-inches, totaling 4- inches.
5. Sidewalks must be restored with like material immediately after pole set.
6. Paving conditions must be approved by Public Works prior to issuance of road opening 
permit.
2. Memorandum from the Planning Director requesting acceptance of the LAND Grant award for
the Magnolia Reserve Conservation project in the amount up to $425,000
Summary of Discussion: Planning Director, Gregg Cademartori stated that this project dated back to
2010 when the City had tried to acquire the land, which were lots at 171 and 281R Magnolia Avenue, R
Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue, with the Trust for Public Lands, but had not been able to
secure grant funding. He stated that the land had been identified in the most recent Open Space Plan. He
stated there was also development proposals on the site currently, but Greenbelt was in talks with the owner
to conserve the area. He stated that Greenbelt had entered into a purchase and sale agreement for the
property and would be the owner of the land, and the City was proposing to purchase a conservation
restriction on the property to ensure the land was conserved in perpetuity. He stated that the Open Space
Committee and the Conservation Commission had both unanimously endorsed the project. He stated that
the motion before the Committee was a comprehensive motion that was required by the State for the
endorsement of the conservation restriction, as well as the acquisition of the conservation restriction. He
stated that the conservation restriction itself had a monetary value, and the City would purchase the
conservation restriction from Greenbelt. He stated that funding for the conservation restriction would be
coming from the LAND grant from the State, Community Preservation Act funds, and private funding from
Greenbelt. He stated that the area was about 94 acres total, and it would link 1,000 acres of abutting
conserved land. He stated that once the funding sources were secured, the closing sale of the property would
happen in late spring.
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 5 of 6
Councilor Grow asked for clarification regarding the funding sources. Julia Fitzpatrick, Land
Conservation Specialist, Greenbelt, stated that Greenbelt currently had a purchase agreement with the
owner of the land for $2 million. She stated that the organization is currently fundraising for the property,
with $120,000 left to fundraise. She stated that Greenbelt had received a $500,000 grant from Mass
Audubon. Gregg Cademartori stated that the conservation restriction would be paid to Greenbelt and
would total $759,000.
Councilor Grow asked what would happen if the fundraising did not meet the needed threshold. Julia
Fitzpatrick stated that Greenbelt had never not been able to fully raise funds for a project. She stated that
the LAND grant was also contingent on the acquisition of the property being fully funded. 
Councilor Kimberley asked for clarification regarding the potential for more funds being needed to secure
the conservation restriction, as outlined in the motion. Gregg Cademartori stated that the funding from
the CPA had not been fully secured, but was likely to be awarded to the project. 
Councilor Gross asked for clarification regarding the cost of the conservation restriction. Gregg
Cademartori stated that there was a cost to placing a conservation restriction which was based on the
appraised value of the property and the removal of development rights.
There was a brief discussion regarding the funding of the conservation restriction versus the acquisition
funding. 
Councilor Grow stated that there is currently a development project for the land before the Conservation
Commission which was a 13-duplex development.
Councilor Gross asked for clarification regarding the contract the City would have with Greenbelt. Gregg
Cademartori stated that Greenbelt would own the property and the City would hold a conservation
restriction on the property that would be administered by the Conservation Commission, and would have
very specific allowed and prohibited uses. 
Councilor Gross asked if any of the property was part of the City watershed. Gregg Cademartori stated
that there are wetlands on the property, but the water drained towards Manchester-by-the-Sea and then out
into the Atlantic, not into the City watershed. 
Councilor Grow asked how the property would interact with the abutting Trustees of the Reservation
property, Ravenswood. Julia Fitzpatrick stated that there were currently trails that lead through the
property to Ravenswood, and once Greenbelt took ownership of the property more formal trail connections
would be established. She stated that there would be a public access plan developed for the property, which
may include parking on the property. 
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor 
Kimberley, the Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to recommend that the 
City Council accept the Conservation Restriction for the Magnolia Reserve Property (171 and 281R 
Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue) as follows:
Ordered: That the Gloucester City Council hereby votes to:
1. Raise and appropriate the sum of $ 759,000, or such other amount as may be necessary, to acquire
a perpetual Conservation Restriction, for the purposes of conservation, protection of wildlife 
habitat, preservation of natural resources, watershed protection, passive outdoor recreation, and
Planning & Development                           November 18, 2026                                 Page 6 of 6
open space, over approximately 94 acres of land known as the Magnolia Reserve Property (171 
and 281R Magnolia Avenue, R Magnolia Avenue, and 607 Western Avenue), located in 
Gloucester, Massachusetts, together with all costs incidental and related thereto. Said 
Conservation Restriction shall be held by the Gloucester Conservation Commission pursuant to 
the provisions of Massachusetts General Laws Chapter 40, Section 8C, and Article 97 of the 
Amendments to the Massachusetts Constitution.
2. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, on behalf of the City, to acquire said 
Conservation Restriction by purchase, gift, bargain and sale, donation, or such other lawful 
means, upon such terms and conditions as the City determines to be in its best interest.
3. Authorize the Gloucester Conservation Commission, the Mayor, and such other municipal 
officers as may be necessary to apply for, receive, accept, administer, and expend grants, gifts, 
reimbursements, and other financial assistance from the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, the 
United States Government, nonprofit organizations, and other public or private funding sources to
defray all or a portion of the acquisition costs. Such funding shall include, but not be limited to, 
assistance available through the Land Acquisition for Local Diversity (LAND) Grant Program 
authorized under M.G.L. Chapter 132A, Section 11, and any successor or related federal or state 
conservation funding programs.
4. Authorize the Mayor, the Gloucester Conservation Commission, and other appropriate municipal 
officials to execute all applications, grant agreements, conservation restriction documents, 
certifications, deeds, and any other instruments or agreements necessary or convenient to 
complete the acquisition and fulfill all grant requirements.
5. Provided, however, that any municipal funds appropriated pursuant to this vote shall not be 
expended unless and until the City has secured all required matching funds, grants, gifts, or other 
contributions necessary to complete the acquisition in accordance with the approved project 
budget.
This authorization is intended to facilitate the permanent protection of the Magnolia Reserve Property as a
significant natural resource for the benefit of the residents of Gloucester and the Commonwealth, 
preserving its ecological, scenic, watershed, habitat, and passive recreational values in perpetuity.
MOTION TO ADJOURN: On a motion by Councilor Kimberley, seconded by Councilor Gross, the
Planning & Development Committee voted 3 in favor, 0 opposed, to adjourn the meeting at 6:35 p.m.
